subject: Personnel controls: onboarding/offboarding artifacts and training roll-out (SOC 2 request)
messages:
From: Galileo Audit <soc2@galileo-audit.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Redwood SOC Team <soc@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Request: personnel controls deliverables for SOC 2 fieldwork

Hi Irene,

As a follow-up to our kickoff, could you please provide the following artifacts by Friday, June 2: 

- Training completion matrix for all employees and contractors for the last 24 months (include training IDs and completion timestamps).
- Redacted background check confirmations for hires from 2026–2028 (redact PII as needed, include verification date and vendor).
- Onboarding and offboarding runbook or playbook that shows the steps and owners for account provisioning/deprovisioning.
- Sample deprovisioning ticket history (last 10 deprovisions) or a log extract showing timestamps and approvers.
- Any attestations or policy documents that cover background checks and training retention policy.

If any of these items are stored in a shared drive or ticketing system, a link + brief navigation notes is fine. Also let us know if contractors are handled the same as employees for background checks.

Thanks,

--
Lena R.
Senior Assoc., Galileo Audit
SOC 2 Engagement Lead
soc2@galileo-audit.com

Lena — thanks for the clear list. We can assemble these. Proposed delivery plan: 

1) Today/Tomorrow (May 29–30): provide training roster CSV (attached) and a redacted sample of third-party background confirmations (attached).
2) May 31: provide onboarding/offboarding playbook (redacted) plus links to the ticketing extracts.
3) June 1: deliver the last-10 deprovisioning log excerpt and retention policy PDF.

Maya — can you confirm the redaction cadence and whether we have contractor confirmations ready?
Jonas — can you prepare the ticketing export from our ITSM for May–June deprovisions and confirm log fields exported (timestamp, approver, requestor, asset scope).

We will use the shared Drive folder (link below) and provide a short manifest with each file and redaction notes. If any item cannot be produced by the date above, we will flag it immediately.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Request: personnel controls deliverables for SOC 2 fieldwork

Irene / Lena — quick status from People ops: 

- Training roster: attached CSV (training_roster_202606-202806.csv). Columns: employee_id, name (redacted id), role, hire_date, training_course_id, completed_at, training_version. We redacted full names/SSNs and replaced them with an internal redaction token.
- Background checks: attached is a redacted sample (bg-check-redacted-sample.pdf) showing verification vendor, check date, scope (criminal/employment), and redaction notes. We cannot include full background reports in the Drive; per vendor agreement we provide verification confirmations and an internal index.
- Contractors: background checks are required for contractors working on access-sensitive projects. We have a separate contractor index; I will export a contractor confirmation list and include it in the Drive by end of day.
- Onboarding/offboarding playbook: draft attached (onboard-offboard-playbook_v1.3.docx). It lists owners (People Ops, IT, Security) and step-by-step triggers.
- Deprovisioning tickets: Jonas will attach the exported CSV of ticket IDs and timestamps. PII is removed; ticket IDs are sufficient for traceability.

Notes on retention: our policy retains training completion records for three years and background verification indices for seven years; the underlying vendor reports are not stored beyond the vendor retention window.

Let me know if you need verbatim vendor letters or an attestation signed by HR.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Manager, People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Galileo Audit <soc2@galileo-audit.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 01 Jun 2028 15:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: personnel controls deliverables for SOC 2 fieldwork

Thanks — this is very helpful. Quick clarifying question: for contractors who receive privileged credentials, do you have the same scope of background checks (criminal + employment verification), or is there a reduced scope? Also can you confirm whether the three-year training retention applies to contractors as well?

If possible, please add a one-paragraph attestation from People Ops confirming scope and retention for contractor records. Otherwise, the artifacts you've described are sufficient for our testing.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

--
Lena R.
Galileo Audit
